newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold sets record volume as banks trade.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold sets record volume as banks trade.

text.p: Active trading led by banks pushed volume to a new daily record of 2,570 kilos on the Istanbul gold exchange on Wednesday.
This compared to a previous daily record of 1,930 kilos on August 26, 1996. Volume was 960 kilos on Tuesday.
Dealers said the main reason fuelling activity was banks making deals in the first session to benefit from price differences between gold prices and the dollar/lira rates.
"The bulk of the trade was made (in the morning) by banks buying in dollar terms and selling in lira terms to record profits," a free market dealer said.
There was 2,490 kilos of trade in the morning session and 80 kilos in the afternoon. 54.7 percent of trade was lira terms.
Gold closed at $356.80 an ounce and 1,263,500 lira per gram, down from $358.70 and 1,265,500 lira at Tuesday's close, in line with world trends.
Dealers said physical gold demand from the free market was not significant although lower prices buoyed purchases.
"Because of the fall in the ounce price, there was a certain amount of physical demand, but most of the demand came from the banks," one bank trader said.
The lira weakened against the dollar to end at 110,010 versus Tuesday's 109,460.
